High-level response and proposed near-term plan:
1) Limited-processor attestation: we can provide a scoped attestation for a narrow processing lane that matches the "session-only telemetry + embeddings" description, provided the scope, retention, and subprocessor list in your sheet are accepted. We'll draft an attestation template and a short operational appendix (what will be logged, how KV cache is isolated).

2) TIA/DTIA evidence mapping: Naomi will map the minimal evidence set (encryption-in-transit & at-rest attestations, subprocessors list & access controls, caching/pseudonymization notes) into a one-page TIA-lite package. Expect an initial draft in 3 business days.

4) Fallback: Jonas — product-side, can we commit to an onshore pseudonymization + cache routing fallback for the pilot? If yes, estimate effort and whether that requires infra change.

- Kimberly and Naomi to review the attached spreadsheet and return an internal decision matrix by EOD 12/11.

Folks — quick legal/readout after a pass on Globemed_DPA_questions.xlsx:

- Limited-processor attestation: acceptable as a commercial mitigation for a time-bound pilot if the scope is tightly limited, retention periods are explicit, and no high-risk categories (health identifiers beyond hashed tokens) are processed. I'll prepare the limited_processor_attestation_template.docx and a short routing appendix.

- UK Addendum / IDTA: our preference is to get the UK Addendum signed when EU <-> UK personal data is involved. However, legally we can accept a TIA-lite + attestation for a pilot if the customer signs an explicit routing exception addendum acknowledging: (a) scope/retention limits, (b) audit rights, (c) reversion to full UK IDTA for production beyond pilot thresholds.

- Subprocessors: we must produce a filtered subprocessors list for the scoped lane (we can redact non-relevant infra providers). Naomi — once you have the TIA-lite draft, we should include the subprocessor snapshot and an access-only attestation.

- Timeline risk: if Globemed insists on the full UK IDTA now, expect a 3-4 week legal review + signature cycle. If they accept attestation + TIA-lite, we can target 7-10 business days to produce docs and sign a routing exception addendum.

I'll aim to upload the attestation template and a short legal note by EOD 12/12. Also CC: I think a DocuSign link (short form) will be best to get signatures quickly.
